narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the length of the loan you requested, your credit history, and your employment situation. The requested loan length was the strongest influence and pushed the decision toward denial. You asked for a 48-month loan, which is more than twice as long as the average 19 months seen among people who were approved. Longer loans carry more uncertainty, so this worked against you.

Your past delays in repaying credit worked in the opposite direction and pulled the prediction toward approval. Even though this history is relatively uncommon (only 5.8% of applicants have it), the model viewed it as a somewhat positive signal compared with other risk patterns.

Your current unemployment also pulled the prediction toward approval. While being unemployed is uncommon in the dataset, the model treated this status as reducing your risk in this specific case.

Taken together, the long repayment period outweighed the other two factors, leading to the denial. To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a shorter loan, updating your credit history with on-time payments, or waiting until you have stable employment. You may also want to review your full credit report before reapplying elsewhere.
